findings.title: AI SDK retry wrappers disable configured failover after initial HTTP 5xx

evidence.detail: Production agent requests set maxRetries: 3, enabling AI SDK transport retries.
streamText spreads streamParams, including that maxRetries value; only OAuth explicitly disables SDK retries at line 1361.
getErrorStatusCode only reads top-level numeric statusCode/status; it does not unwrap AI_RetryError.lastError.
Configured backup requires isFailoverEligibleError(error), which receives the wrapper.
A wrapper with no top-level status is ineligible for failover.
Documented 5xx behavior is retries followed by configured failover.

findings.trigger: An ordinary agent request (maxRetries: 3) receives initial HTTP 503 responses whose message is 'Provider unavailable'; defaultModel=local/primary and failoverModels=['local/backup'].
findings.consequence: Observed actual AI SDK/adapter path makes four primary HTTP requests, throws AI_RetryError with lastError.statusCode=503 but classifierStatus absent, and makes zero backup requests. This is not the intended Openbuff outer retry/failover policy; UI attempt/status telemetry cannot see the inner retries either.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one retry owner for all provider request paths (prefer the Openbuff loop with AI SDK maxRetries: 0), preserve the last provider error/status in a canonical error contract, and classify failover on that contract.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use the offline HTTP fixture from evidence/02-providers-probes.test.ts, probe http-retry-wrapper-disables-failover: primary returns HTTP503 + Retry-After:0, backup streams text. Require bounded primary attempts followed by one backup attempt, final success, and accurate retry/failover status events.

findings.title: In-band SSE error status is converted into prose instead of retry metadata

evidence.detail: createOpenAICompatibleStreamError embeds code/status/details into Error.message but only assigns name; it does not retain status/statusCode properties.
The production SSE adapter uses that converter for error chunks.
The stream loop throws that converted Error for non-tool errors.
Retry/failover status extraction only reads numeric properties, not embedded message JSON.
Existing 'preserves structured provider metadata' regression checks message contents rather than retry-classifier-visible status.

findings.trigger: A configured provider opens HTTP200 SSE and emits {error:{message:'Upstream provider failure',code:'upstream_error',status:'503'}} before any content, with a configured backup.
findings.consequence: Observed real SDK stream receives OpenAICompatibleStreamError, classifier status is absent, and performs one primary request with no retry or backup, despite an explicit server-error status in the provider payload.
findings.suggestedFix: Normalize validated numeric/string status into a structured numeric statusCode and preserve provider code/details separately from the display message. Reuse the same error contract as HTTP failures.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run the sse-status-loss fixture through the production configured model and AI SDK. Require classifier status503 and the documented bounded retry→backup behavior before any content is delivered; malformed status must remain unclassified.

findings.title: Default streaming transport drops usage and suppresses configured cost accounting

evidence.detail: stripProviderMetadata defaults true for OpenAI-compatible providers.
CLI/SDK configured OpenAI-compatible providers use the local OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel.
That production constructor always sets includeUsage: undefined; config exposes no includeUsage control.
The usage request field is sent only when includeUsage is enabled.
On a tool-calls finish, the default adapter terminates the stream before later usage chunks.
Both provider cost extraction and configured-pricing fallback are inside !stripProviderMetadata.
If cost fallback does run without token counts, computeCostCentsFromUsage treats missing usage as zero.
Reported cost is accumulated into step accounting.
The usage callback unconditionally feeds cache totals and token-calibration observations.
The green late-usage test explicitly constructs includeUsage: true, unlike the shipped constructor.

findings.trigger: A real configured OpenAI-compatible stream uses pricing input=$3/M, output=$15/M and offers usage 20,000 input +10,000 output tokens. A tool turn sends usage after finish_reason=tool_calls; separately a normal text turn sends known usage with stripProviderMetadata=true.
findings.consequence: Observed tool stream delivers its tool call but loses all offered usage; with metadata stripping disabled the cost callback reports0 instead of21 cents. With the default stripping flag enabled, a text stream retains usage but never calls the cost observer at all. Cache/calibration inputs and step cost therefore lack truthful provider provenance. Actual provider charges and hard budget enforcement were not measured by these probes.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate request-metadata compatibility from response accounting; negotiate include_usage for supporting endpoints and retain terminal usage when requested; represent unknown usage/cost distinctly from zero. Keep high precision internally and round only for display. Attach provider/model/currency/provenance to accounting.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use late-tool-usage and strip-provider-metadata-cost-gate fixtures with the real configured adapter. Both must report21 cents with 20k/10k usage, preserve exactly one tool call, and report unknown rather than0 when the endpoint supplies no usage. Test endpoints that reject include_usage via an explicit compatibility control, and assert runtime aggregates receive the same receipt.

findings.title: Context preflight requires backup credentials before a healthy primary can run

evidence.detail: Context resolution is documented as capacity-only without touching credentials.
It scans every primary/failover candidate and calls credential-validating resolveConfiguredProviderModel.
A matched backup with missing apiKeyEnv throws synchronously.
The production agent loop calls the resolver before its first programmatic step.
The stream path also calls it before entering the guarded provider attempt loop.
CLI readiness validates the selected root provider, so the primary can pass readiness before this backup error.
Failover is documented as secondary and starts only after primary request failure.

findings.trigger: defaultModel=local/primary is an unauthenticated local provider with a valid200k window; failoverModels includes backup/emergency with HTTPS endpoint and an unset apiKeyEnv.
findings.consequence: Observed getModelForRequest successfully constructs the primary, but capacity resolution and promptAiSdkStream throw the backup missing-key error before any fetch. A dormant emergency route takes down the otherwise usable primary.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve route/model capability metadata without credential validation; check credentials when a candidate is actually selected. Surface invalid backup readiness separately, with a defined skip/fail behavior when failover is needed.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use context-preflight-backup-credential-coupling fixture. Require primary window200k and a successful primary request with backup credentials absent. If primary fails, require a precise backup configuration result without erasing the primary failure.

findings.title: Configured reasoning effort is omitted for custom OpenAI-compatible provider IDs

evidence.detail: Configured route effort is resolved and exposed on ModelResult.
withConfiguredReasoningEffort writes providerOptions.openaiCompatible and providerOptions.openai.
The adapter's providerOptionsName is the configured provider ID.
The generic options namespace read by the adapter is 'openai-compatible' (hyphenated), followed by the provider ID.
reasoning_effort is emitted only from the options it parsed.
Template effort uses the same camelCase namespace, so the generic route shares the mismatch.

findings.trigger: A custom provider ID 'local' declares reasoning support and high/medium/low efforts; defaultReasoningEffort='high'; a normal agent stream is sent through the actual configured adapter.
findings.consequence: Observed ModelResult.reasoningEffort is high while the HTTP body has no reasoning_effort. Providers named 'openai' can use the other namespace, making behavior depend on the arbitrary configuration ID rather than declared capabilities. Adaptive role choices can likewise be selected but never transmitted.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish one canonical generic provider-options namespace and use it consistently at producer/adapter boundaries, or map options using the resolved provider ID. Preserve compatibility with existing public option names and validate effort support.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use reasoning-provider-options-namespace fixture; run high/medium/low route and template overrides for provider IDs local, custom-gateway, and openai. Require the same correct wire reasoning_effort or an explicit unsupported-setting result.

findings.title: Configured OAuth routes ignore the skip flag used for recovery

evidence.detail: The resolver receives skipChatGptOAuth.
A configured chatgpt-oauth provider is selected unconditionally; skip/rate-limit flags are checked only in the later implicit OAuth branch.
Only implicit OAuth honors skipChatGptOAuth and the rate-limit cache.
The OAuth rate-limit recovery recursively calls the same params with skipChatGptOAuth:true to obtain configured provider fallback.
Failed auth refresh uses the same skip-based fallback.
Non-streaming requests also rely on skipChatGptOAuth:true.
Existing test checks the policy helper's skip behavior, not actual configured model selection.

findings.trigger: defaultModel='codex/gpt-5.5', provider codex type chatgpt-oauth; recovery or a non-streaming caller invokes getModelForRequest with skipChatGptOAuth:true.
findings.consequence: Observed actual model resolver still requests OAuth credentials and returns isChatGptOAuth:true. Thus the recursive recovery path can revisit the same excluded provider instead of selecting BYOK backup. A known configured OAuth rate limit is not prevented by the cache in that branch. The probe injected credentials and did not exercise real refresh/subscription services.
findings.suggestedFix: Define explicit OAuth recovery routing: honor skip for configured routes, select only configured BYOK backup candidates, and fail with an actionable reconnect/route message when none exists. Make rate-limit state apply to configured OAuth routes too.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use configured-oauth-ignores-skip fixture plus a simulated pre-content429/failed-auth-refresh recovery. After skip is requested, neither OAuth credential getter nor backend fetch may be called again; configured BYOK backup must run or an actionable terminal error must result.

findings.title: Streaming retry bypasses the shared deterministic-error policy

evidence.detail: The shared classifier fails fast for content-policy errors and explicit non-retryable statuses, and extracts bounded Retry-After.
Streaming normalizes content-policy errors but does not call the shared classifier afterward.
Streaming accepts transient message OR retryable status OR empty stream; a policy error retaining503 is consequently retried.
Streaming always computes exponential delay rather than applying the shared Retry-After decision.
Non-streaming uses runWithRetryPolicy, so policies diverge.
The retry matrix tests the correct helper, not the production streaming gate.

findings.trigger: An injected provider stream fails before output with createProviderContentPolicyError({statusCode:503}); the shared classifier says retryable:false.
findings.consequence: Observed promptAiSdkStream makes four stream attempts and three backoff calls while the shared policy requires one. Deterministic refusals can consume extra requests and delay, and the streaming layer does not share the documented header-aware decision. The four attempts are Openbuff outer stream calls in this DI probe; they are distinct from the four internal HTTP retries in02-F1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use classifyRetryableError in the streaming gate, with the explicit no-content and empty-stream exceptions retained. Apply its delayMs and cancellation semantics. Combine with a single retry owner so policy is checked before hidden SDK retries.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use stream-loop-bypasses-shared-retry-classifier fixture. Require one call/no backoff for policy503 and non-retryable400 containing transient-sounding text; require bounded Retry-After for429, no retry after user abort, and existing safe buffered-tool retry/failover regressions to remain passing.

domainAssessment.security: Reviewed provider schema validation, HTTPS credential transport, loopback-only unauthenticated HTTP, ancestor-source trust stripping, readonly-root provenance and no-hosted-fallback boundaries. No new concrete exploit was validated in this lane. Project/explicit provider config is deliberately trusted; discovery, credential persistence and arbitrary tool permission security are not fully re-audited here.
domainAssessment.correctness: Real routing/stream/tool paths are present. Offline production probes establish status-wrapper/SSE normalization gaps, usage/cost loss, backup credential coupling and configured reasoning/OAuth control mismatch. Advisory tool metadata is distinguished from operational provider compatibility.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Pending tool buffers reset per attempt; delivered-content gate prevents unsafe replay; cost/cache observers use step-local accumulators; CLI send ownership protects authoritative completion; backoff/diagnostic listeners clean up. OAuth rate-limit state is process-global and configured routes do not honor it; config cache returns shared mutable data and fragmented atomic-write scopes were inspected without a crash/concurrent-writer test.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Finite request/post-stream bounds and shared header-aware retry helper are strong existing infrastructure. Production streaming bypasses that helper, HTTP SDK wrappers obscure status, in-band errors flatten status, and OAuth skip recovery does not select a different configured transport. Suggested fixes retain delivered-content safety.
domainAssessment.performance: Assessed tool/stream buffering, synchronous config dependency discovery, metadata waits, retry multiplication/wrapper effects and diagnostics worker-pool wiring. Cache invalidation rediscovering fragment files is deliberate. No throughput/latency/RSS measurements or known-vulnerability assertions are made.02-F7 demonstrates avoidable retry calls without fabricating timings.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: SDK declares ai and pinned @ai-sdk/anthropic; internal package declares @ai-sdk/provider/provider-utils and ai with compatible V2 interfaces. Shared workspace packages are deliberately bundled. Semver ranges and manifest declarations were inspected; registry/CVE/lock integrity and published dist were outside this lane. Installed AI SDK retry wrapper source was inspected only as probe context, excluded from native receipt.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: 62 existing tests passed across retry policy, tool buffering, cost helper and the two adapters;9 offline current-behavior probes passed. These expose production wiring failures despite green helpers. OAuth tests are classifier-only; metadata error tests assert prose rather than classifier properties; usage test enables an option never enabled by the production constructor. No real API/live provider, CLI TUI end-to-end or OAuth refresh test was run.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Checked provider config, compatibility controls, shared StreamChunk/truncation shape, CLI status consumer and configured routing docs. Failover after5xx and reasoning effort differ from production behavior. Per-model tools/caching metadata is advisory. Legacy-window helper and specialized OpenRouter/failover-floor helpers are not default runtime capabilities. OutputTokens precedence and output-byte diagnostic scope are documented limitations.

coverageLimits: Receipt covers41 inventory files with64 exact sampled/merged ranges; large provider/run files were not audited line-for-line. Selected picker ranges were read, with adjacent production consumers added.
Read-only source audit; only owned /tmp reports and offline probe artifacts were created. No source implementation or source test files were changed.

Nine offline probes pin CURRENT observed behavior. Their passing result is reproduction evidence, not acceptance that these defects are fixed.62 existing tests passed separately under pinned Bun1.3.5.

No external API calls, credential/private provider configuration values, private logs or secret environment values were inspected. Config fixtures and the OAuth credential function response were synthesized.
Installed node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs retry/error source was consulted for probe interpretation; not included as a current inventory source in structuralReceipt.

Provider discovery transport, OAuth credential persistence/real refresh, Responses transformer internals, embedding generation and API-dependent concurrent/subagent e2e tests were not fully reviewed in this lane.
Native Openbuff query_index/read_files/coverage tools are not exposed in this Codex session; discovery used picker artifacts, rg and exact numbered reads. Root will run native receipt validation.
Capability quality is not model intelligence/accuracy. No provider benchmark, cost accuracy measurement or claim of best possible performance is made.
Automatic benchmark-to-routing learning/measurement producers were not traced across evals; existing /models recommend is an opt-in configured evidence lookup.
